text: Hezekiah sent word to all Israel and Judah, and he also wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh, inviting them to come to the house of the LORD in Jerusalem to keep the Passover to the LORD, the God of Israel.
The king and his officials and the whole assembly in Jerusalem had decided to keep the Passover in the second month,

versions.text: For the king and his officials and the whole assembly in Jerusalem had agreed to keep the Passover in the second month,
versions.explanation: The Hebrew begins a new narrative clause ("took counsel"), not a subordinate explanation of verse 1. Opening with "For" leaves verses 2-3 without a main clause and makes the report of the decision in verse 4 sound repetitive. A plain declarative statement reads more naturally aloud and follows the Hebrew structure.

text: since they could not keep it at the proper time: not enough priests had consecrated themselves, and the people had not gathered in Jerusalem.
The plan seemed right to the king and to the whole assembly,

so they resolved to send a proclamation throughout Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, calling the people to come to Jerusalem and keep the Passover to the LORD, the God of Israel; for they had not kept it in great numbers as it is written.

So the couriers went throughout Israel and Judah with letters from the hand of the king and his officials, and by the king's command they said: "People of Israel, return to the LORD, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, that he may return to the remnant of you who have escaped the hand of the kings of Assyria.
Do not be like your fathers and your brothers, who were unfaithful to the LORD, the God of their fathers, so that he made them an object of horror, as you yourselves see.

Now do not stiffen your necks as your fathers did. Give your hand to the LORD and come to his sanctuary, which he has consecrated forever, and serve the LORD your God, so that his fierce anger may turn away from you.

For if you return to the LORD, your brothers and your children will find compassion with their captors and will come back to this land. For the LORD your God is gracious and merciful, and he will not turn his face from you if you return to him."
The couriers went from city to city through the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and as far as Zebulun, but the people laughed at them and mocked them.
Yet some from Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem.
In Judah too the hand of God was at work, giving them one heart to carry out what the king and the officials had commanded by the word of the LORD.
A great crowd gathered in Jerusalem to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread in the second month—a very large assembly.
They set to work and removed the altars in Jerusalem, and they took away all the incense altars and threw them into the Kidron Valley.
They slaughtered the Passover lamb on the fourteenth day of the second month. The priests and Levites, put to shame, consecrated themselves and brought burnt offerings into the house of the LORD.
They took their accustomed places as prescribed in the Law of Moses, the man of God, the priests sprinkling the blood they received from the hand of the Levites.
For many in the assembly had not consecrated themselves; so the Levites had to slaughter the Passover lambs for everyone who was not clean, to consecrate them to the LORD.

For a great many of the people—many from Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun—had not purified themselves, yet they ate the Passover contrary to what is written. But Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, "May the LORD, who is good, make atonement for everyone

versions.text: For a great many of the people—many from Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun—had not purified themselves, yet they ate the Passover otherwise than it is written. But Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, "May the LORD, who is good, make atonement for everyone
versions.explanation: "Otherwise than it is written" is stiff and unclear when read aloud; "contrary to what is written" conveys the same sense (eating without the prescribed purification) in idiomatic English.

text: who sets his heart to seek God, the LORD, the God of his fathers, even if he is not clean according to the purity of the sanctuary."
And the LORD listened to Hezekiah and healed the people.
The people of Israel who were present in Jerusalem kept the Feast of Unleavened Bread seven days with great joy, and day after day the Levites and the priests praised the LORD with loud instruments.

versions.text: The people of Israel who were present in Jerusalem kept the Feast of Unleavened Bread seven days with great joy, and day after day the Levites and the priests praised the LORD with loud instruments of praise to the LORD.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has "instruments of strength/loud instruments"; "of praise" is added content. The doubled "praised the LORD ... to the LORD" is also clumsy for oral reading in English, since the divine name has already been supplied as the object of the praising.

text: Hezekiah spoke encouragingly to all the Levites who showed skill in the service of the LORD. So they ate the festal meal for the seven days, sacrificing fellowship offerings and giving thanks to the LORD, the God of their fathers.
Then the whole assembly agreed to keep the feast another seven days, and they kept those seven days with joy.

For Hezekiah king of Judah contributed a thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep to the assembly, and the officials contributed a thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep. And a great number of priests consecrated themselves.

The whole assembly of Judah rejoiced, along with the priests and the Levites, and all the assembly that had come from Israel, and the foreigners who had come from the land of Israel or lived in Judah.
There was great joy in Jerusalem, for since the days of Solomon son of David, king of Israel, there had been nothing like it in Jerusalem.
Then the priests and the Levites stood and blessed the people, and their voice was heard; their prayer came to his holy dwelling place, to heaven.

versions.text: Then the Levitical priests stood and blessed the people, and their voice was heard; their prayer came to his holy dwelling place, to heaven.
versions.explanation: Throughout this chapter priests and Levites are consistently named as two groups (vv. 15, 16, 21, 25). Rendering the phrase here as "the priests and the Levites" keeps that consistency and matches the likely sense in Chronicles; "Levitical priests" narrows it unnecessarily.
